WASHINGTON · 02:38 UTC

Federal agents subpoenaed Rep Ilhan Omar's relatives in probe of her immigration record

Federal immigration law bars most noncitizens from entering the United States if they have provided material support to a designated terrorist organization. Once inside the country a foreign-born person can apply for lawful permanent residence and later but only after disclosing all past affiliations and travel history on the required forms. Congress members enjoy no exemption from federal scrutiny of their own immigration records.
The seek records that could show whether any family member supplied false information about Omar’s age or background when she first arrived from Somalia in the 1990s or when she adjusted her status years later.
